methodology: Authorized runtime route and schema verification. HTTP method existence was primarily proven with unauthenticated GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests that stop at Lucky authentication; method discovery does not execute protected mutating handlers. Selected GET routes were additionally verified with the repository OpenToken client. Request schemas were recovered from frontend pass-through/object literals and, where applicable, cross-checked against authorized read-only GET shapes. For the final six Docker legacy wrappers that lacked current UI call sites, the user explicitly authorized isolated schema probes: upgrade/build used dedicated disposable BusyBox resources, Git/ZIP/import used validation-failure paths, and prune was exercised only by a temporary Lucky instance connected to a non-destructive mock Docker API. No real Docker prune handler reached the production Docker daemon.

same_bundle_prefix_artifacts.description: Literal-only paths that are strict prefixes of method-bearing routes from the same frontend bundle. Runtime probing confirmed no additional standalone method beyond already cataloged generic/template matches; PATCH probes were also 404. Suppression is version-bound and is not performed by the generic extractor.

no_route_literals.description: Unauthenticated GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH all returned route-not-found semantics on Lucky 3.0.0.
